tasks: Determine whether four distinct primes can be divided into two pairs with equal pair products.
Give a mathematical justification of the existence judgment.

independent_solution.result: No such four distinct primes exist.
independent_solution.proof: Suppose distinct primes p,q,r,s satisfy p*q=r*s. Then p divides r*s, so by prime divisibility p divides r or s. Since r and s are prime, this means p=r or p=s, contradicting distinctness.
independent_solution.alternative_proof: Unique prime factorization of the equal product forces the unordered factor multisets {p,q} and {r,s} to be equal, which is incompatible with four distinct primes.
independent_solution.qualifier: The statement is about two disjoint pairs from four distinct primes; non-prime integer counterexamples do not establish prime existence.

source_reviews.coverage_expectations: Retain primality, four distinct values, the two-pair partition, and a justification of the negative existence judgment.
